q-37821.name: Question 1
q-37821.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243863/assets/d51a8e78f8b8c1f05e502bd98aed6a253799336765f1331d23e63ec637bcb448.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
q-37821.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243863/assets/438ce908c902696b480bf9791cae089be40f9e7b2552208e13e08405496b696c.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{7}{16}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}} \\  & =\pm \frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we select the positive answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So our final answer is $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{4}.$

Question 1

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the x-coordinate of the point P is 74, use the Pythagorean identity to find sin⁡θ.

a
34
b
−74
c
−34
d
34
e
74
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Any point (x,y) on the unit circle is related to the central angle θ as follows:

x=cos⁡θ,y=sin⁡θ

We're given that x=74 at the point P. Therefore, we have

cos⁡θ=74.

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find sin⁡θ:

sin2⁡θ+cos2⁡θ=1sin2⁡θ=1−cos2⁡θsin⁡θ=±1−cos2⁡θ

Substituting cos⁡θ=74 gives

sin⁡θ=±1−(74)2=±1−716=±916=±34.

Finally, we select the positive answer since sin⁡θ is positive in the first quadrant. So our final answer is sin⁡θ=34.

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{15}}{5},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta .$
q-65064.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243863/assets/44a555d222e3f6ff85208e8722a728ad240c558de7982d2a480bf9ddfb23ac6f.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{\sqrt{15}}{5}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{15}}{5}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{15}}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{15}}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{15}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{10}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}.$

Knowing that $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5})}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{10}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{10}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{10}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{10}}{10} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-65064.html:
Question 3
?

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the x-coordinate of the point P is 155, use the Pythagorean identity to find csc⁡θ.

a
5
b
105
c
52
d
102
e
5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Any point (x,y) on the unit circle is related to the central angle θ as follows:

x=cos⁡θ,y=sin⁡θ

We're given that x=155 at the point P. Therefore, we have

cos⁡θ=155.

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find sin⁡θ:

sin2⁡θ+cos2⁡θ=1sin2⁡θ=1−cos2⁡θsin⁡θ=±1−cos2⁡θ

Substituting cos⁡θ=155 gives

sin⁡θ=±1−(155)2=±1−1525=±1025=±105.

We select the positive answer since sin⁡θ is positive in the first quadrant. So, sin⁡θ=105.

Knowing that csc⁡θ=1sin⁡θ, we have

csc⁡θ=1(105)=510.

Finally, we rationalize the denominator. csc⁡θ=510=510⋅1010=51010=102
